research_question: Among people with cancer receiving radiotherapy, with or without concurrent chemotherapy, what is the effect of probiotics compared with placebo on the incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea?
treatment_label: Probiotics administered during radiotherapy (with or without chemotherapy)
control_label: Placebo administered during radiotherapy (with or without chemotherapy)
outcome_description: Incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea during radiotherapy or the study-defined follow-up period, based on a recognized toxicity grading system or an author-defined threshold that is clearly equivalent to grade 2 or higher.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means probiotics reduce the incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea compared with placebo and therefore favor probiotics.
search_queries: probiotics placebo radiotherapy cancer diarrhoea trial
probiotic controlled chemoradiotherapy cancer grade 2 diarrhea
probiotics radiation induced diarrhoea cancer quantitative comparison
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of people with cancer receiving radiotherapy, with or without chemotherapy, that evaluate a probiotic intervention against placebo.
Studies reporting the incidence or sufficient quantitative information about grade 2 or higher diarrhoea, or a clearly equivalent moderate-to-severe diarrhoea threshold.
Studies involving any cancer type, radiotherapy technique, probiotic species or formulation, dose, treatment duration, setting, language, publication status, or participant age.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded.
No comparison between a probiotic treatment condition and a placebo control condition.
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size; extractable means and SDs, t/F-values, proportions/event counts, or odds ratios are required.
Completely unrelated to probiotics, cancer radiotherapy, or treatment-associated grade 2 or higher diarrhoea.
moderators_to_extract: Cancer type and anatomical radiotherapy field
Use of concurrent chemotherapy and chemotherapy regimen
Probiotic formulation, species/strain composition, dose, and duration
Diarrhoea grading system and outcome-assessment time point
Participant characteristics and baseline risk, including age and prior gastrointestinal comorbidity
effect_size_note: Treat the endpoint as dichotomous and extract numbers of participants with grade 2 or higher diarrhoea and total participants by arm wherever possible; also capture reported adjusted or unadjusted relative effect estimates and confidence intervals when event counts are unavailable. Harmonize toxicity definitions so that only grade 2 or higher, or a clearly equivalent threshold, is included. Orient all effects so positive values favor probiotics. Use one eligible estimate per independent sample in the primary synthesis, address multi-arm studies without double-counting placebo participants, and examine alternative grading definitions or assessment windows in sensitivity analyses.
single_outcome_target: incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea
